visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a medium shot of a woman with long dark hair and glasses (Lady Flavor) gesturing towards the camera while standing next to a man. They are positioned behind a wooden table where a white illustrated calendar sits. The background is a clean white studio wall. (2) A close-up reveals the calendar's cover, titled "2026", featuring colorful cartoon illustrations of cats and dogs engaging in activities like hot air ballooning, camping, and swimming. The man's hands hold the calendar, showcasing its design. (3) The man, wearing glasses and a grey sweatshirt, takes a more central role, gesturing expressively with his hands as he explains the product's features. The camera cuts frequently between the speakers and close-ups of the calendar's internal pages, which contain comic-style art. (4) A brief cutaway shows a real tabby cat yawning on a grey surface, providing a thematic link to the product. (5) The man demonstrates the calendar's utility by flipping through pages, revealing specific dates like "April 28" accompanied by illustrations and text. The editing is rapid, using jump cuts to maintain high energy. (6) They introduce a variety of merchandise sets, including small calendar cards, bookmarks shaped like cat heads, and a black T-shirt with a complex graphic on the back depicting a podcast setup. (7) A brown, cat-faced pouch is shown in detail, with a woman's hand opening its zipper and placing a small white device inside. A smartphone is then tapped against the pouch, demonstrating a tech feature. (8) The video concludes with the duo holding a large canvas tote bag and the pouch, waving to the camera. The final shot is a close-up of a small metal pin of a surfing cat held near a dog's nose.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A bright, upbeat acoustic guitar melody begins immediately, setting a cheerful tone. A female voice speaks with high clarity and a friendly, rising intonation, introducing the brand and the new 2026 calendar product. (2) A rapid series of paper rustling sounds occurs as the man flips calendar pages, synced with the visual action. The male voice enters with an energetic pitch and fast speech rate. (3) A digital "pop" sound effect triggers as a text overlay appears on screen. The BGM remains consistent in tempo and volume, providing a steady rhythmic floor under the dialogue. (4) A subtle "whoosh" sound effect accompanies a scene transition while the man's vocal delivery remains enthusiastic. (5) A distinct "zip" sound is heard as the pouch is opened, followed by a short, high-pitched digital notification chime when the phone interacts with the pouch. (6) The voices overlap briefly during the call to action, followed by a final swelling of the music volume before a clean fade out.
